newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Access Economics sees Australian rate cut chance.
newsitem.headline: Access Economics sees Australian rate cut chance.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia is likely to ease monetary policy again if the economy does not begin to move towards four percent annual growth, economics consultancy Access Economics said on Wednesday.
"Another cut still cannot be ruled out," Access said in its June Economics Monitor.

"If evidence accumulates the economy is not accelerating to the desired four percent per year growth rate, while wages growth and inflation remain acceptable, logic says the Reserve Bank would cut again," Access said.
"So more short interest rate cuts depend on evidence economic growth is still anaemic," it said.
Access said interest rates would start to rise again when wages growth accelerated or if there was evidence that the economy was picking up too much pace.
Australia's gross domestic product grew 0.9 percent in the March quarter from the previous quarter to stand 2.4 percent above its level a year earlier.
The Reserve Bank has eased monetary policy four times in less than a year, each time by 0.5 percentage points.
The latest interest cut, on May 23, was prompted by a belief that inflation was not a concern and anecdotal evidence that the economy was still struggling, Access said.
The bank's overnight cash-rate target fell to 5.5 percent.

Access forecast business investment to weaken over the 1997/98 financial year to June 30, meaning a pick-up in economic growth would have to flow from an improvement in the housing market and private consumption.

"While business investment was strong in the March quarter, the expectations survey suggests growth will slow in 1997/98, weakening one of the current growth forces in the economy," it said. "A pick-up in housing and private consumption would then be vital if demand growth is to continue."
